proof_ledger.name: Artie Ficial
proof_ledger.motive_before_vote: Monet, will that check clear before Friday? Grant wanted his name over the door, a vote in every department, and my resignation. Sue objected to the terms. Six years here. I had written the introduction for the man replacing me. Our savior, I wrote. It's in my pocket. I keep reaching for it.

That's how well I was handling it. Still tidying up after him. Claire, I kept smiling because I couldn't think what else a host was supposed to do.
proof_ledger.final_claim_before_vote: Would somebody take over the tables? Intake took the bottle off the support before the guests entered. They left the label. I had refused the donation and sent the refusal to the board. Grant could still stand up and announce whatever he liked. I was going to have to stop him in front of everybody. There were enough decisions left to defend without leaving a filled bottle in that room. Could somebody please take the tables?

proof_ledger.name: Claire O’Scuro
proof_ledger.motive_before_vote: The bowl's ownership papers were incomplete. I approved its label too soon; Grant retained my signature. Reed kept asking me to revisit it. Grant wanted the explanation brought to him personally. I put his copy beside the glass at his place. He was elsewhere. I remember moving the glass to keep its damp base off the paper. Such a small, fussy thing to remember. Reed, I was angry enough to let him wait for his explanation afterward.
proof_ledger.final_claim_before_vote: An empty historical bottle. That is what I authorized for the preview, and what the incoming sheet says. The papers went to intake in the course of catalog work. Reed, put the old bowl label down. I know what it says. I signed it. I would like to answer for that decision without being made responsible for a filled vessel I never approved.

proof_ledger.name: Hugh Bidder
proof_ledger.motive_before_vote: Grant wanted a refund on the Star Bowl and a public admission that its certificate was false. My firm supplied it. I changed our file instead of admitting we'd been fooled. Elon began worrying about his other purchases; Saul was available to help him worry. My settlement wasn't enough. Grant wanted the admission tonight. Some of you knew me before I had a respectable office. He meant to send me back there.
proof_ledger.opportunity_before_vote: I kept the seller's correspondence out of the auction handouts. Bowl and bottle, both purchases. Grant had demanded one refund already. I brought the retained file to his private place to settle it quietly. His glass was there; he wasn't. I took my file away again. Saul, you can call that evasive. I wasn't having a dealer dispute performed for your collectors. A client says refund softly enough and somehow everybody hears it.
proof_ledger.final_claim_before_vote: The seller's instructions changed before delivery. Empty the original liquid; replace it with an inert substitute. Grant's declaration described that delivery. Intake kept the older attachment. The bowl certificate was false, and I altered our file. I have answered for that purchase. The bottle was a different transaction. Elon, your files are available through my attorney. Tonight they stay closed.

proof_ledger.name: Monet Bags
proof_ledger.motive_before_vote: Friday. That's when wages are due. My mother used to wait by the phone on payday. I know what that does to a household. I'd moved money to pay our staff. Grant wanted the books before releasing his check, and the board wanted answers too. Artie hated losing authority. I had transfers to explain and no time left to explain them.
proof_ledger.opportunity_before_vote: The manager brought the cheese ticket to accounts. I crossed out our account and sent Grant's copy back. I went to his private place for a signature too. His glass was waiting; he wasn't. I stayed with the unsigned bill, then returned to accounts. The restricted transfer was still off the board agenda. He wanted my books before releasing his donation. I wanted him to pay one of his own bills.
proof_ledger.final_claim_before_vote: I went to get Grant's signature before the preview. His bare glass was already beside the invoice; he wasn't there. I left his copy and returned to accounts. The cheese argument came later. So did another request for money we didn't have. The restricted transfer was my decision. If you want it undone, tell me which member of staff to ask for their paycheck back.

proof_ledger.name: Chip Patina
proof_ledger.motive_before_vote: Recent repair. Not ancient. Grant wanted ancient on the label. He had the insurance copy with the date I altered. I said no. I picked up the waiting glass to look at its engraving and put it back. Then the alcove mount moved. I went there. Frank's entrance had to close. The insurance copy stayed where it was.

A photograph of the band work doesn't inventory every scrap in the room. The insurance date is mine. I changed it. Leave both sheets on the bench. Leave the strips where they are. I need to be able to find my own things.

proof_ledger.name: Dada DiCapo
proof_ledger.motive_before_vote: Vincent, tell them whose jacket it was. Nobody's. Empty jacket, gilded chair, my film: Donor Collapse. Grant's foundation wanted to acquire it with my name removed. Getting anyone to look at my work took years. He expected thanks for erasing me from it. I was going to make that room uncomfortable. I can't bear the title now.
proof_ledger.opportunity_before_vote: I went into the private room for the coordinator. Showed her the jacket film on my phone. She said no. After she left I tried the angle from Grant's chair. His glass was waiting. An empty chair and a waiting glass: he'd made himself a stage. I wanted the screen on during his toast. I was going to make my own work impossible to ignore.
proof_ledger.final_claim_before_vote: The studio film was the rehearsal. Grant was going to fall after the private toast. He'd rejected the advertised program, but we still had the private live version agreed. I thought he'd get up and demand an apology. I had an answer ready for that. I wanted him to hate it. That's the answer. Switch it off.

proof_ledger.name: Vincent Van Faux
proof_ledger.motive_before_vote: He kept exhibiting the early picture. My breakthrough, apparently. I painted it to pay rent. Now he wanted the bottle study printed beside his rescue announcement. I withdrew permission; he could hold my final payment. Hugh told me to be less difficult. Dada, you kept making new work. Grant could buy another picture from me and still introduce me as the boy who painted his first.

Later I took Grant's unsigned reproduction release to his place. His glass caught the light there, too. He wasn't around. I left the release beside it. Hugh, you could sell the arrangement. My painting wasn't a signature on every object you put beside it.

proof_ledger.name: Sue Venir
proof_ledger.motive_before_vote: He intended to announce the gift before a board vote. Its terms gave him approval of future acquisitions. He also had the ownership file carrying my earlier advice. proof_ledger.opportunity_before_vote: Artie and I stopped the announcement at the public desk. I kept the running order; my earlier advice was attached to the transaction. I also went to Grant's private place for his donor copy. The glass stood on it. I lifted the glass and pulled the paper free. You can see why I'd want that copy. Mona, I was short with you. I lifted the glass, pulled the paper free, and stayed during the pour. That is the visit I described. Private hospitality remained on my public running order. Mona's letter is a separate question; she can answer for it herself.

proof_ledger.name: Dr. Art E. Fact
proof_ledger.motive_before_vote: Reed found a gap in my ownership citation. Grant could expose it whenever I withdrew authority from his catalog. proof_ledger.name: Tess Tament
proof_ledger.motive_before_vote: Family gift for the photograph. His gift when I asked for a say. I asked Sue about the succession clause. Please give me a minute before the next question.

Ask me about my work; leave that person alone.

I can still see where it ought to be.

I wasn't reopening it to save his photograph.

Chip was right about the missing calculation, and I kept arguing. I would still like that chair moved back. Apparently every detail I got right is now going to be treated as another mistake.

He wasn't there. I put it under the edge of his waiting glass to keep it on the table. I wanted him to read it without a roomful of people helping him laugh. Sue may object to the stationery when I've finished.

The letter needed a clearer attribution, and Tess deserved an answer about my commission. She can decide what to do with that information. I was there when he chose the water. I would like someone to answer the claimants now.

Later I tried the panel beside Grant's waiting glass, where he would use it. He was elsewhere. I'd committed money before Monet agreed to a trial. proof_ledger.motive_before_vote: My old memo permitted lender descriptions before the papers caught up. Grant had my signature and wanted it as precedent for his gift. I took it out of the display file. People ask me to stand by the founding plaque and remember something charming. He had found the memory I was ashamed of, and he meant to use it to buy the rest of the museum.

Then I went to Grant's place to leave him the memo instead. He wasn't there; the glass was. I didn't leave the memo. I stood there reading my own name on it. Artie, I know I no longer run the place. You needn't tell me again tonight.

My old policy is in the file beside the one that replaced it. You can read both. I kept that key when I left. Apparently even a useless key is too much of this place for me to keep.

proof_ledger.name: Saul D. Bid
proof_ledger.motive_before_vote: Grant circulated Hugh's valuation beneath my house's name. I had accepted an advisory fee. He could require me to defend the price and return the fee before my own clients. I withdrew the comparison. Hugh and I have known each other a long time. Being made to answer for his transaction was a humiliation Grant understood perfectly well before arranging it.

Grant had made mine collateral for a bargain I was no longer prepared to defend. That was the conversation I meant to have.
proof_ledger.final_claim_before_vote: Intake removed the bottle before the collectors entered. The card stayed beside the painting. We carried out the withdrawal physically. Hugh was perfectly capable of selling his own valuation without my house's name beneath it. I know he took the withdrawal personally. I intended him to. Being obliged to remain civil has never meant that I liked the transaction.

proof_ledger.motive_before_vote: That fabric cost another client's advance. I told Grant when I asked for early payment. He would fill the hole if every future use of my pattern became his. proof_ledger.opportunity_before_vote: Frank closed the alcove. I unfastened my top panel because the lamp was too close. Production kept the pattern slides. I carried the panel through the private room and rolled it beside Grant's waiting glass. He was elsewhere. The advance has gone back; my client thinks it was a delay. Grant knew where I'd spent it. He could keep his unsigned pattern transfer. I was taking my work home. The bottle looked like another projected shape in that light. I had given production pattern slides, not an inventory of the bench.
proof_ledger.final_claim_before_vote: Production projected the bottle between the pattern slides. The physical loan stayed in the cupboard. People remember the lit shape beside my fabric. The pattern is still mine, and the other advance has gone back. My client thinks her payment was delayed. Grant knew where I'd spent it. She thanked me for returning it. I'm not reading her message to this room.

proof_ledger.name: Reed DeLabel
proof_ledger.motive_before_vote: I found the missing document. I changed the bowl entry. Grant wanted settled ownership put back. He could make my correction a publicity stunt and my doctorate the museum's embarrassment. Claire, it's the same chapter. Again. I've stopped telling people which draft I'm on. I'd like you to read the finding before deciding what you think of me.
proof_ledger.opportunity_before_vote: I kept both bowl labels and shortened the bottle entry. Intake kept the full query and purchase attachment. Grant wanted every correction approved, so I took the short caption to his private place. He wasn't there. I laid it beside the waiting glass and took it away again. The program couldn't get longer and the donor couldn't look foolish. I was supposed to find wording that satisfied both.
proof_ledger.final_claim_before_vote: I deleted a credit line. The original-contents sentence was not the cut. Senior staff had the purchase attachment at intake. I shortened the attribution and corrected the bowl wording. Both were my decisions. Claire, please let me get to the end of one answer without starting it over because someone important has frowned.

proof_ledger.name: Al Baster
proof_ledger.motive_before_vote: Cold-cast resin with metal powder. Publicity said solid bronze; I let it stand. Grant could expose the difference, cut my final payment, and make his name bigger than mine. I've got somebody at home who needs help getting up the stairs. He enjoyed discussing how grateful I ought to be for a commission while he held the money I needed from it.
proof_ledger.opportunity_before_vote: I refused a replacement and crossed out solid bronze. Frank closed the alcove; the contracted piece was already installed. After the bottle preview I went to Grant's private place about my last payment. His glass was set out. I sat beside it. Nobody came, so I left. I wasn't making him a second sculpture for free or paying another crew to remove the first.
proof_ledger.final_claim_before_vote: The red scrap came off my sculpture. Red-faced leaf with a silver back. I cut it for the entrance piece myself; it travels when you work with it. I corrected the bronze description. Is there a quiet place I can call home? Someone is there with mine tonight. I can't answer for every scrap while they wait for me.

proof_ledger.name: Ella Gance
proof_ledger.motive_before_vote: I withdrew my approval. Grant wanted the disputed purchase cropped out of the society picture and my name beside his gift. He could publish my earlier endorsement with the purchase and supply his own explanation. Elon can look comfortable in any photograph. I work harder at it. Grant meant to show everyone exactly how hard, if I ceased being useful.
proof_ledger.opportunity_before_vote: I asked to leave the disputed object out of the photograph. The photographer supplied a crop and kept the original. I attended the preview. Later I went to Grant's place to tell him which picture he could release. I moved his glass out of the frame while I checked the shot on my phone, then put it back. He wasn't there. A flattering photograph had become his proof that I approved of him. I wanted that stopped before morning.
proof_ledger.final_claim_before_vote: The original photograph was at Grant's private place, by his toast table. Public gallery was the export designation. I went for that photograph and never returned to an unattended glass. I withdrew my endorsement afterward. He could have printed my change of mind. I am not going to praise him because he is dead.

proof_ledger.name: Drew Conclusions
proof_ledger.motive_before_vote: I praised the rescue before there was a rescue. Grant's agency paid for advertising. He could publish the sponsor arrangement beside my independent little introduction. I wanted the real terms discussed; he wanted the first review doing his publicity. I liked being invited early. He knew that. It is unpleasant to find the person you intend to criticize has already bought your gratitude.
proof_ledger.opportunity_before_vote: I replaced the post with the terms and removed the sponsor credit. The jacket teaser had a clatter under it; Paige got the full export. I took my phone to Grant's private place to show him the revised post. Waiting glass, no Grant. I sat there replaying the old favorable version. He'd kept that one. I could edit mine all night; his screenshot would still exist. Do you know how sick you get of hearing your own voice doing the pitch?
proof_ledger.final_claim_before_vote: I used gala audio under the studio jacket footage. The sound is Grant collapsing before the toast. His trouble had started before he drank from the gift glass. Excellent episode timing. You can hear how I'd have introduced it. The sponsor paid for advertising around my review. Please don't ask me to say the title again.

proof_ledger.name: Brie DeVivre
proof_ledger.motive_before_vote: Has everybody eaten? I'm asking seriously. I'd bought Grant's extra cheese course without funded authorization. Monet held the charge; the supplier wanted my money; he wanted the plates out. The private toast was already paid. I wanted one person outside the kitchen to say no. He knew whose bill it would become. You don't usually hear about those.
proof_ledger.opportunity_before_vote: The manager came back about the cheese charge. I showed the order: addition disputed, toast paid. I took the culinary flavoring to Grant's place and later left the container with service. I'd already bought the addition without funding. The supplier was waiting for my payment. Cheese does not get cheaper while two offices decide whose bill it is.
proof_ledger.final_claim_before_vote: My container stayed closed. The manager had put the flavoring into the shared pitcher that supplied the toast. I left the container with service. Dinner was still cooking. The cheese is still on my bill. Monet, we can fight about it tomorrow. Tonight my staff need coats and rides home. Somebody get them those before asking for another plate.

independent_exhibits.title: The prepared place and delivered toast

proof_ledger.name: Cary Crates
proof_ledger.motive_before_vote: I cracked a frame corner on delivery. Wrote old damage. Grant had the photographs. He could send them to my employer or have me sign without another check. I lost a job once with my coat still on the peg. Haven't forgotten it. He knew that call could finish my work here. He enjoyed letting me decide which signature would postpone it.
proof_ledger.opportunity_before_vote: Took the shop gifts to service. Freight lift stuck. Al's crew wanted their balance. I corrected the frame-corner report. Grant still had the first version, so I went to his private place to get it back. Glass set out. Nobody home. I waited, picked up the shop carton to clear the chair, then left. Great night for deliveries. If you need a chair moved, ask. I'd rather do that than stand here answering for the word old.
proof_ledger.final_claim_before_vote: The crest glass stayed boxed. Service used a plain spare for Grant's drink. Signing for a carton doesn't mean unpacking it. The frame corner was my damage. I've signed the corrected report. Don't call my employer for me. Give them my number and I'll answer. Is that everything about the delivery?

independent_exhibits.title: The prepared place and delivered toast

proof_ledger.motive_before_vote: I'd promised school places before the grant was approved. I'd put back the school program he crossed out. I wanted him to see it before he stood up to be thanked for his generosity.
proof_ledger.final_claim_before_vote: The private place was part of the group tour. I stayed with the group throughout it. The new handout was my doing. The visits still need funding. That money won't appear because I insist children deserve to come here. I'm still going to insist.

proof_ledger.name: Faye Stop
proof_ledger.motive_before_vote: Grant wanted my originals. One showed him with the bowl consultant he denied meeting. His agency had the commercial retouch I'd passed off as editorial. He could ruin my credibility with it. I keep one last picture of someone I loved. It's badly lit. He wanted me to hand over a real moment so he could decide who was allowed to see it.
proof_ledger.opportunity_before_vote: Ella's crop went to the agency. I kept the whole gallery frame and the preview image. Barb kept outside crews out of the private room. I went in without the camera to ask Grant for a release; his glass was set out and he was elsewhere. I waited. Later I photographed the delivered toast from the public reception. He looked at the lens. I said half an inch. He moved. I keep hearing myself giving him that stupid little instruction.
proof_ledger.final_claim_before_vote: I added the bottle to the preview export. It wasn't in my original wide frame; they'd withheld the physical loan. Publicity wanted a complete-looking arrangement. The corrected commercial retouch is a separate file. Stop watching my hands. I know they shake. Put the pictures on the table if you want to look at something.

proof_ledger.name: Robin Banks
proof_ledger.motive_before_vote: I wanted a hearing for the claimants. Grant wanted applause first. I threatened to disrupt the announcement. He could have security exclude me and call that protecting the museum. Barb has removed me before. I remember the door closing. Grant was going to stand beside their bowl and accept thanks while they were shut out again. I wasn't willing to leave politely.
proof_ledger.opportunity_before_vote: I distributed the petition after security warned me. At intake I kept the ownership card with it. I interrupted Paige's interview and gave Grant a copy. I'd seen the bottle at the preview. Later I went to his place with the petition's signature page. Glass on the table, nobody listening. I put the page down, then took it back. He wasn't keeping people's names for his own collection. Barb, I wanted an answer. You know how many times we'd already asked.
proof_ledger.final_claim_before_vote: The recorded petition exchange was by the public podium. That's where I interrupted and gave Grant his copy. My later signature-page visit was separate. The bowl card is still inside my petition. Return it intact or hear the claimants: that's the demand. It is still unanswered. His death is not an answer. Stop looking at me as though you expect me to be pleased.

independent_exhibits.title: The beginning of the press interview

proof_ledger.name: Penny Pincher
proof_ledger.motive_before_vote: Please don't pass the family handout around. I removed it. I bought their shares using a damaged example, though ours was intact. Then I paid a dealer much more for another work. Grant wanted both figures in the handout. They trusted me with the family things. Paying them back wouldn't stop him showing what I'd done. I haven't called them.
proof_ledger.opportunity_before_vote: I removed the price comparison from the handouts. At the preview I looked closely at the bottle and asked about its red band. Later I went to Grant's private place to discuss the family valuation. His glass was waiting; he wasn't. I put my own copy of the comparison down beside it and stayed a while. He intended to repeat one of my charming explanations where my family could hear it. I wanted to know what that silence was going to cost.
proof_ledger.final_claim_before_vote: Around the neck. A loose price collar, not a band across the stopper. The drawing concerns the support treatment. A split collar doesn't mean someone opened the bottle. My family has the payment difference now. Grant could still show them the original dishonest comparison. They haven't called. I keep checking my phone under the table. Could we get to the next question?

proof_ledger.name: Justin Tyme
proof_ledger.motive_before_vote: The Stolen Museum. Great headline. The tenant-trust settlement made it less great. Grant could use my omission to dismiss the deed, the missing payment, the whole folder. He wanted the records and confidentiality with the retraction. Anne, you know me. I start with a folder and somehow end up telling it like I was there. He could make the storyteller the reason nobody listened.
proof_ledger.opportunity_before_vote: I gave counsel the deed and settlement together and circulated the Velvet Widow clipping. Grant wanted the property folder, so I took it to his private place. His glass was waiting. I stayed to write a note, tore it up, and took the folder away. He could discredit every record by telling people what my headline omitted. I'd handed him the best line in his rebuttal.
proof_ledger.final_claim_before_vote: The editor's follow-up says the contents were neutralized before transfer. The deed's in Sue's folder with the later settlement. Anne, I'll give you the whole story another day. I don't have a story to tell you about this.

proof_ledger.name: Minnie Malist
proof_ledger.motive_before_vote: Restraint was the brief. Then Grant wanted a reveal, a tribute, another photograph. I'd ordered additions before Monet approved them. The crew balance was mine. He could cover it if the production became his, or leave me owing it while he took his photograph. I say yes and work out how later. He knew exactly how much that habit would cost me tonight.
proof_ledger.opportunity_before_vote: I kept the revised running order after the screen piece was canceled. The first styling plan put a transparent hood over Grant's place. Service got the revised sheet; I kept the crew copy. I checked the place myself while nobody was there and shifted the glass an inch to center it. It was still somehow my job to make his evening look effortless. Brie, remember when our problem was bad lighting? I'd like that problem back.
proof_ledger.final_claim_before_vote: Turn the music off. The hood stayed over Grant's glass until the manager collected it. The cancellation was for the alcove; the clear space in the photograph is a reflection through the cover. The crew balance is mine. Somebody needs to tell them what's happening. Leave the lights up. I'm finished trying to make this room flattering.
